title: Nicheformer published in Nature Methods — a foundation model for single-cell and spatial omics
subtitle_or_tagline: The spatial-transcriptomics pretraining substrate matures from preprint to peer review
topic: Fabian Theis announces the Nature Methods publication of Nicheformer, a transformer foundation model pretrained across single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data. Nicheformer bridges the two modalities by learning a shared representation space, allowing existing single-cell atlases to be projected into spatially-aware contexts and providing a pretrained substrate that downstream spatial models (including niche/microenvironment predictors) can fine-tune from. It consolidates the lab's earlier line of work on reference-mapping and niche prediction, and positions itself as infrastructure for the spatial-omics model ecosystem alongside tools like CONCERT.

osiris_connection: Nicheformer is the substrate layer of the spatial-omics stack that OSIRIS's spatial cards model. The OSIRIS connection is about transfer under a bound: a foundation model pretrained on dissociated single-cell data is being displaced (fine-tuned) into the spatial regime, and the representation drift between modalities is exactly the Δx that Theorem 7 bounds. A norm-clamped fine-tuning regime (L*c on embedding updates, per the OSIRIS lens) would make the single-cell→spatial transfer certifiable: the model may use its full displacement budget where the spatial context genuinely demands it, but cannot drift arbitrarily far from its pretraining distribution. This is also the monitoring round's planned maturation: the 18:00 round flagged Nicheformer as a watch item; peer-reviewed publication is the promotion criterion met.
